findings.issue: d (A-2: default-range combos / 1326 x 100, before dead cards) is never asserted against an independent number. AC#2 computes the expected width with the same rangeWidthPct the implementation uses, so a broken rangeWidthPct (counting classes / 169, counting after dead-card removal, or dividing by the wrong total) leaves every test green.
findings.evidence: rangeWidthPct appears only as the oracle in AC#2 (line 133) and inside estimateOpponentRanges (src/advice/ranges.ts:319, 610). No test pins a concrete value. Recomputed: UTG open-raise default = 162 combos = 12.217...%, BB check = 90.35%.
findings.fix: Add a unit assertion with a hand-computed value, e.g. rangeWidthPct(new Set(['AA','AKs','AKo'])) toBeCloseTo((6+4+12)/1326*100, 9), and in AC#2 or the unit file assert the typical estimate's widthPct for the UTG open-raiser equals the default classes' summed comboCount / 1326 * 100 computed in the test (no rangeWidthPct call), on a view whose dead cards intersect the default range so the 'before dead cards' rule is exercised.

findings.issue: The min(n, 100) cap (spec section 7 edge case 'n > 100 is capped at 100') has no test that can fail. All formula and AC#6 cases use n = 30 or n = 100, where removing Math.min gives identical results.
findings.evidence: scaledWidthPct(20, 60, 100) = 60 with or without the cap; AC#6 uses hands: 100. No test uses n > 100.
findings.fix: Add a unit case scaledWidthPct(20, 60, 250) toBeCloseTo(60, 9) (and optionally an estimateOpponentRanges case with hands: 150 giving the same widthPct as hands: 100).

findings.issue: Only open-raise (PFR) and call-raise (VPIP) have their stat choice verified by width. limp is checked only for its basis, and three-bet, four-bet and call-three-bet are untested, so a wrong entry in OBSERVED_LINE_STAT (src/advice/ranges.ts:556-564) for those lines would pass.
findings.evidence: limper assertion checks basis.observedHands only (line 213); no view with a 3-bet/4-bet line in the new tests.
findings.fix: In the LIMPED case assert limper.widthPct equals scaledWidthPct(d, vpip, 50) with vpip != pfr; optionally add a three-bet view asserting the PFR stat.

findings.issue: ranges.ts now imports basisText from explain.ts while explain.ts imports OBSERVED_MIN_HANDS from ranges.ts, creating a module cycle and making the range model depend on the explanation layer. It works today only because neither value is used at module top level.
findings.evidence: src/advice/ranges.ts:11 import { basisText } from './explain'; src/advice/explain.ts:17 import { OBSERVED_MIN_HANDS } from './ranges'.
findings.fix: Import TYPICAL_PLAYER_BASIS / OBSERVED_BASIS from './explanations' in ranges.ts and build the text there (or move basisText into ranges.ts and re-export), so ranges.ts no longer imports explain.ts.

findings.issue: Poker plausibility: the order is exactly reproducible (all 169 entries recomputed, 0 mismatches) and the top and bottom are sound (AA 85.5, KK, QQ ... 42o, 32o 32.1; values within ~0.3 of published equity-vs-random tables). But the measure ranks offsuit gappers with one high card above suited connectors: K2o #87 > 87s #99, Q2o #108 > 76s #116, J2o #123 > 65s #128, T2o #135 > 54s #136. A loose observed caller (VPIP 40-60 %) therefore gets Q2o/J2o-type hands before 76s/65s, the opposite of how loose limit players actually play. The justification and range-model.md do not mention this known bias. Separately, the task-mandated PFR-for-all-raising-lines rule widens three-bet/four-bet ranges to the player's PFR (e.g. UTG four-bet default 2.56 % -> 18 % for an ordinary 22/18 player at 100 hands); this follows the task text but is unrealistic.
findings.evidence: Recomputed hand order via computeEquity: matches the file. Positions from the stored list as above. Default widths: UTG four-bet 2.56 %, UTG three-bet 3.77 %.
findings.fix: No code change required for this round (D-1 and the per-line stat rule were user-accepted). Add one sentence to the justification/range-model.md noting that all-in equity vs a random hand understates suited connectors relative to offsuit high-card hands, and raise a follow-up task to reconsider the hand order measure and the PFR scaling of three-bet/four-bet ranges.

summary: Implementation matches the spec: formula (d + (o-d)*min(n,100)/100), A-1 prefix with AA floor and 1e-9 tolerance, A-2 width before dead cards, PFR/VPIP by line with check unscaled, 30-hand threshold, per-opponent basis ascending by seat, snapshot validation with exact RangeError messages, non-array snapshot ignored (block 1c), unseen mode ignores the snapshot without validation, adviceOptions unchanged so bots never see it, load-time hand-order validation reporting every problem, lead clause lower-cases 'Your'/'You' correctly and keeps sentence counts, locked re-pins are additive with counts kept. hand-order.json recomputes exactly for all 169 classes. Gaps are test strength: rangeWidthPct is only used as its own oracle, and the n > 100 cap has no test that can fail. Minor: stat-per-line coverage, a ranges<->explain import cycle, and an undocumented bias of the equity-vs-random order against suited connectors.
